To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tensile properties of additively-manufactured Ti-6Al–4V can be predicted by a constitutive equation that accounts for the microstructure of the material and the effect of texture on tensile strength.

1) the yield strength of Ti-6A1-4V can be accurately predicted using constitutive equations, 2) the constitutive equations are nominally the same for three different heat treatments (stress relief, hot isostatic pressed, and β-annealed), and 3) the constitutive equation predictions are within 5% agreement with experimental measurements.

the tensile yield strength of Ti-6-4 produced via directed energy (i.e., powder bed) additive manufacturing is predicted to be a function of the microstructural features, including the volume fraction of α phase, the grain size, the texture, and the amount of retained β phase.
